answer: Admission uses a delayed postal challenge as the only inlet: the network mails a sealed nonce to a unique street address that is not already registered and not a shared virtual-mailbox lagoon. After the carrier scan, the operator has a short window to photograph the opened card beside a live challenge. Each address binds to one identity; reuse is rejected on a public registry and the deposit is slashed. A farm cannot mint names from servers: it must lease a distinct address, wait out delivery, and appear in person for every clone, so cost stays high even at the nadir of cheap rented rooms.
